svg.title: Vector-symbolic binding
svg.desc: Left: three words bound to roles by XOR on 64-cell bit strips, folded into one summary by majority vote; unbinding with role 1 gives a strip that matches word A far above chance and words B and C near chance; a curve shows cross-talk noise growing with the number of bundled items, about 8 times below the signal at 64 items in 4,096 bits for random codes. Right: three ways to choose a word's code and their held-out change in bits per byte: fixed hash codes helped, root codes with 120 values gave no gain, and root plus residual codes were worse than fixed.
svg.text: Vector-symbolic binding: glue with XOR, merge by vote, compare by counting
Bind, bundle and probe on 64-cell bit strips
matching cells out of 64, for the strips drawn (chance is 32)

signal is about 8 times the noise.
not a measurement on this model.

Dots and clumps are illustrative (mode 1 draws 120 clumps).
Negative bits per byte is better. 2 seeds, 2 held-out slices, older CPU learner (now barred by D24): parked.
The strips and noise curve illustrate the mechanism, not this model.
